=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves emerge from the same node, visible in multiple images; 3-5 leaves per node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes, especially at shoot apex)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin without teeth; some minor irregularities likely due to damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to apex and base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with lateral veins branching off perpendicularly)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced closely, numerous (clearly visible in close-up images, forming a reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, not exceeding leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is light to medium green, consistent with young growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky sap visible upon damage or breakage)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: [NOTE] Multiple images show the same seedling from different angles. The leaves are arranged in whorls at nodes, with 3-5 leaves per node, and exhibit a glossy, elliptic shape with entire margins. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes and yellowish spots), likely environmental or minor herbivory, but not extensive. The stem is herbaceous, green, and smooth. No stipules, latex, pulvinus, or tendrils are visible. The overall morphology is consistent across all images.
